_comment: Coinbase Derivatives contract sizes, pinned rather than fetched.
WHY PINNED: the funding parser computed notional as contracts * price, which is
correct only for a contract whose unit is one unit of the underlying. No Coinbase
Derivatives contract is. Twelve HBAR contracts at $0.0802 is $4,812 of notional,
not $0.96, and every field the parser derived from that number - APR, the 8h
equivalent, the hourly rate, the regime classification - was wrong by the
multiplier, which for HBAR is 5,000x.
WHY NOT FETCHED AT BUILD TIME: coinbase.com returns 403 to every automated agent,
and the CFTC product-certification filings that would be the primary source are
scanned images with no extractable text. Every multiplier below therefore comes
from secondary reporting, corroborated across independent outlets, and every one
of them carries its sources so the claim can be checked rather than trusted.
STATUS IS PART OF THE DATA. `verification` is 'secondary' on every row here and
nothing in this repository has yet read a number off the exchange itself. Running
scripts/check_contract_specs.py against a session that can reach Coinbase is what
promotes a row to 'exchange' and stamps `verified_on`. Until then the terminal
says so on screen: a pinned multiplier is labelled pinned, not confirmed.
A SYMBOL THAT IS NOT IN THIS FILE HAS AN UNKNOWN MULTIPLIER, NOT A MULTIPLIER OF 1.
Defaulting to 1 is what produced the original error. The parser refuses to compute
a notional it cannot justify, in the same way the sizer refuses to size an asset
with no recorded volume.

No nano Hedera contract was found in any source. The review that prompted this file called the 5,000 HBAR contract a nano; the multiplier is the same either way, the product name is not, and the name here is the one the sources actually use.
The CFTC filing (ptc04032518912.pdf) is a scanned image and could not be read as text; 500 XRP is corroborated across two independent secondary sources instead.
